title: 6th Sitting of Third session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened with 33 members present. After two written ministry answers to South Hulhumale' questions, members debated a petition from law students against the Bar Council's new rules for qualifying law degrees (exams in person at a centre, even for online students); most speakers backed finding a fix for students already enrolled. They then began a second petition, asking that MPs' health insurance be cut, with PNC members saying they would support cutting it and others arguing the cost to the state is small and the petition's comparisons misleading. After a recess, two bills/resolutions had first readings announced, the Economic Committee's report on the Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation nominee was debated, and debate on a foreign-relations report on the disability-rights Optional Protocol was just starting when this part ends; no votes were taken in this part. This part covers the debate on the foreign relations committee's report on joining the Optional Protocol to the UN disability rights convention, then the continuing debate on a petition asking for the health insurance MPs get to be cut because the public does not get it. Several members raised points of order during the petition debate, and the chair said that debate would carry on at the next sitting. The Majlis then voted to approve the appointment of Alfadhil Ahmed Shafneez as Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation (55 yes, none against) and to let the Maldives join the Optional Protocol (64 yes, none against). The text layer is garbled in places, so some speech summaries are approximate.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked the housing minister for the total money needed to finish ongoing projects and what is set aside this year.
Asked how many airports are being upgraded and how much more money is needed to finish them.
On the law-degree petition, cited an Auditor General report on the state-funded degree scheme and said degrees need clear qualification standards.
Said unequal treatment exists across society, including in health cover and in how courts treat people, and that this should be weighed when looking at the petition.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Backed the petition and tied MPs' pay, allowances and insurance to how well the Majlis performs.
Said the minority's voice must be heard alongside the supermajority and objected to the chair limiting his remarks.
Linked the petition to proposed amendments to the Majlis rules affecting members' protections.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Called the petition important; said students enrolled under old terms should not be affected and institutions should arrange a way for them to finish.
Raised a point of order about members being described as hired members.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said students at several colleges had been told they would not need a set centre; the change forces island students to travel and should be revisited with them.
The chair told him to sit down and observe the Rules before he resumed his turn.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Said rules should not be applied backward to students who enrolled under earlier terms, and the petition's concerns need a solution.
Said PNC members support cutting state spending and argued the petition's comparisons with other countries were selective.
Said false claims about insurance money for his family had circulated on social media.
Said the facts of the insurance scheme should be explained clearly to the public.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: On the insurance petition, welcomed the public petition portal and said PNC members would support cutting MPs' insurance if the public wants it.
Said MP insurance costs the state about MVR 26,000 per MP a year and warned such petitions can sow division between public and MPs.
On the tax-authority report, supported it and the committee's choice.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said state bodies and other countries insure officials, that Aasandha covers all citizens, and that the petition's comparisons mislead.
Raised a point of order about how another member had spoken of fellow members and their pay.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said the Bar Council may set rules, but applying a new in-person exam rule to enrolled online students, such as police officers on islands, adds heavy burdens.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the rule requiring half the assessment as controlled exams forces online students to travel; pointed to MQA guideline and offer letters and urged full recognition of existing students.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said students enrolled and spent money before the change; asked that the committee bring the affected parties together to find a solution.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: As a former Bar Council member, said the Council can add module requirements but should consult students and give those already studying a fair outcome.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Said the petition carries thousands of signatures; opposed one-hall exams for online students and asked for a practical way to sit exams.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shamin Habeeb
positions: Said the decision was not well studied and creates hardship for students; asked the Bar Council to review it without removing existing students' rights.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Said the petition and the Bar Council's reforms both have merit but a mid-course change hurts students; asked for a workable arrangement for them.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Questioned whether the Bar Council's model suits courts applying Islamic law and urged a review of the change in consultation with students.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked that debate time go to any MP who wants to speak rather than by party, and said an independent audit should set MPs' benefits.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Backed cutting MPs' insurance if the public wants it, noting Article 102 lets the Majlis set benefits and citing US and Japan arrangements.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Said MPs' cover is small next to Aasandha costs, that he has no objection to cuts, and that claims of large benefits are misleading.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report: two candidates met the criteria and the committee recommends Ali Fazil Ahmed Shafneez after a 96.20 percent interview score.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report recommending the Maldives join the Optional Protocol to the disability-rights convention, with no extra state cost.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Backed the committee report; noted the Maldives ratified the disability convention in April 2010 and said the protocol lets individuals bring complaints to the UN committee.
Welcomed the government's decision to join the protocol and said it adds to accountability.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aslam
positions: Raised a point of order on the previous speaker's remarks about corruption cases involving state leaders and court rulings.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Backed the petition and called for equal health insurance for all citizens, not only MPs.
Said the state should study the costs and audit them before deciding.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 1 to 3 of the third session of 2026 declared accepted
Mauroof Zakir moved to the Economic Committee and Ameen Faisal to the Judiciary Committee
Proposal to amend Rule 191 sent to the General Committee
Debate on the law-degree petition closed without a vote
First readings announced for the diplomatic privileges and immunities bill and the Raasmale agreement resolution
Debate on the Economic Committee's tax-authority nominee report closed; vote not in this part
The Majlis approved the appointment of Alfadhil Ahmed Shafneez (S. Hulhudhoo, Bageecha) as Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, 55 votes in favour and none against.
The Majlis approved the Maldives joining the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and submitting its instrument of accession, 64 in favour and none against.
The chair ended the day's debate on the health insurance petition without concluding it; it continues at later sittings.
The next sitting was set for Tuesday 20 October 2026 at 9:00.

votes.what: Approval of Ahmed Shafneez as Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation (56 present)
Joining the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (65 present)
